## Motivation

Add long-context agentic launch recipes and their recorded performance evidence to the existing GLM, Inkling, and DeepSeek cookbook pages.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, and DeepSeek-V4 agentic sections; add model-local agentic sections and deployment-panel links for GLM-5.3-Flash and Inkling. The diff touches **five existing model pages**, with no new pages or navigation entries.
- Add **12 model/GPU/TP recipes**, labeled collapsible commands, hardware/runtime prerequisites, and qualification notes. Preserve the explicit 1,048,576-token context limit for the six Inkling/DeepSeek recipes.
- Keep each model's evidence beside its recipes: **128 full-precision records**, 35 historical comparison groups, 42 SGLang 0.5.21 concurrency points, and four recorded GPQA comparisons. Collapsible catalogs retain configuration, runtime, workload, source-checksum, and qualification identities.
- Include the measured GLM-5.3 public-image command with its exact image digest and checkpoint revision, distinguishing its parser-off measurement from the parser-on recipe.

The placement follows the model-local agentic subsection in merged [#46825](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46825). These workload-specific recipes have different runtime, checkpoint, or launch conditions from the generic Deploy cells. Existing configuration/benchmark JSX and generated InferenceX data retain their established workload and verification status; historical custom-runtime measurements are not promoted into public-runtime benchmark cards.

## Accuracy Tests

The SGLang 0.5.20 campaign summaries report paired GPQA-Diamond evaluations, **five runs of 198 items per arm**:

| Selected recipe in its measured runtime | Speculation on | Speculation off |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 / B200 TP4 | 0.738 | 0.757 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 / H200 TP4 | 0.741 | 0.760 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 / B200 TP8 | 0.7434 | 0.7202 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 / H200 TP8 | 0.7495 | 0.7384 |

These are recorded historical summaries, with decision-receipt checksums included; raw per-item GPQA outputs are not retained in the CSVs. They do not qualify the changed SGLang 0.5.21 settings, larger context windows, tool calling, or multimodal behavior. No new GPU accuracy tests were executed for this documentation change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The model-local evidence preserves output tokens/s/GPU, mean ITL/TTFT, concurrency, replicate counts, errors, exact image identities, and client/workload settings. Historical averages include every retained repeat. The SGLang 0.5.21 tables retain all seven concurrency points per measured configuration, including the Flash B200 outlier and recorded request errors.

- SGLang 0.5.18/0.5.20 measurements use actual speculative verification where enabled, on synthesized hash-trace prompts with `ignore_eos`.
- All 42 recorded SGLang 0.5.21 points use simulated acceptance; these numbers do not qualify the natural-acceptance public launch commands.
- GLM-5.2 shortened-output results, GLM-5.3 parser differences, Pro's heterogeneous client settings, and the unmeasured GLM-5.3-Flash variant remain explicit.
- Custom-runtime digests and trace hashes identify measured artifacts without making them publicly downloadable. Public stock-image results remain separate controls.

Validation performed:

- Cookbook authoring checks and all **52 cookbook tests** passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed on all five changed model pages.
- `mint validate` and `mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passed with the CI-pinned **mint@4.2.559**.
- All 12 recipe commands and the historical public-image example passed `bash -n`; 62 distinct flags and 24 parser uses matched pinned upstream source.
- Independent reconciliation verified all 128 records, 35 aggregates, 42 source-file hashes, and configuration/protocol joins.
- All five model pages rendered in the browser, all 12 launch accordions and four model-local evidence catalogs expanded, the new deployment-panel section buttons were present, and no browser runtime errors occurred.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The public-checkpoint recipes have not been freshly launched or benchmarked on the current upstream revision. This remains a draft; the model-local evidence distinguishes measured configurations from public-runtime adaptations.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Changed-file hooks pass.
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Not applicable to this documentation-only change; existing cookbook tests passed.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Recorded results and their scope are included; no new public-runtime GPU qualification is claimed.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

Model Introduction **GLM-5.2** is Z.ai's flagship Mixture-of-Experts model built on **DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)**: a lightning indexer selects a sparse set of key tokens per query (top-2048), so attention cost stays near-constant as context grows. FP8 is the recommended deployment; BF16 (~1.5 TB) needs an 8×B300 node or a multi-node setup. For Blackwell, NVIDIA also publishes an **NVFP4** build (`nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`) that quantizes only the MoE experts' linear weights and activations to 4-bit (the shared expert stays unquantized), holding accuracy within ~1 point of the FP8 baseline on GPQA Diamond, SciCode, and IFBench.  ## 1. Model introduction
 
 GLM-5.3-Flash is a natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model built around a hybrid attention architecture — 320B total parameters with 18B active. Its 45 text layers combine MLA attention, DSA sparse attention, and KDA linear attention, and a 24-layer vision encoder handles image and video input. The checkpoint uses 288 routed experts with 8 active experts per token and includes a native MTP draft layer for speculative decoding. See the [GLM-5.3-Flash blog](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3-flash) and the [GLM-5 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15763) for training details.

Model Introduction **GLM-5.3** is Z.ai's flagship Mixture-of-Experts model built on **DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)**: a lightning indexer selects a sparse set of key tokens per query (top-2048), so attention cost stays near-constant as context grows. It keeps the same base architecture while updating post-training for complex coding and long-horizon tasks. It ships in two precisions — **FP8** (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`) and full **BF16** (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`) — both with **78 transformer layers**, **256 routed experts** (8 active per token), a **1M-token context window**, and a single **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)** layer for built-in EAGLE-style speculative decoding. FP8 is the recommended deployment; BF16 (~1.5 TB) needs an 8×B300 node or a multi-node setup. For Blackwell, RadixArk publishes an **experimental NVFP4** build (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, Model Optimizer) that quantizes only the routed experts' linear weights and activations to 4-bit (attention, shared experts, dense layers, MTP, embeddings, and the LM head stay unquantized), cutting the weight footprint to ~0.45 TB so a 4-GPU GB300 node can serve it with TP4. **The NVFP4 cells are experimental** — benchmark data (accuracy / throughput) is still pending; treat them as provisional until the benchmark cards fill in.

Model Introduction **Inkling** is a Mixture-of-Experts model from Thinking Machines — **975B** total parameters, **41B** active per token, with a **1M-token** context window and **open weights** (BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints below). It handles text, image, and audio inputs natively, and exposes a **variable reasoning-effort** control to trade latency and cost against answer quality. This page covers serving Inkling on SGLang, including its **MTP** speculative-decoding path and long-context prefix caching (unified radix cache + HiCache).
